title: Local bath feedback leaves residual response; the matched comparison shows no advantage
status_authority: Exact selected source bytes and scoped source reports are preserved. This incremental integration does not promote correctness, novelty, physical capability, priority, or practical advantage.
reported_status: The selected Ultra checkpoint and later local-only addendum report bath-mediated logical-record erasure using own-port/own-spin feedback without broadcast. The addendum changes the residual expression and must remain a later source version. A later warm/compact matched comparison reports that a cold no-receiver case has stronger retained entanglement than the hot-receiver case at the same target phase, so the tested model does not show an advantage.
scientific_scope_status: Under the supplied bath and receiver model, own-output feedback removes a dominant response but leaves a residual cross-response; the addendum reports local-only control with no broadcast. The later compact/warm comparison reports a bright-phase temporal quadrature and explicit collection/filter efficiencies, while a missing hot direction retains an O(n) residual. In the matched target-phase comparison, source-reported negativity is about 0.467930 for cold/no receiver and 0.406866 for hot/receiver. This is a negative advantage result within the model, not a physical experiment.

proof_availability.classification_scope: Both original and later addendum source versions and the subsequent comparison artifacts are retained. The optimizer correction and source-reported checks are not independently replayed here; native output access and calibrated readout remain unacquired.
